title: Lattice plugin manifest
description: A plugin teaches Lattice something new — a syntax, a fence — that works on any slide. Components that are designed around a plugin declare it in their own manifest's `plugins` block; a plugin never names a component. The manifest declares WHAT it contributes and whom it depends on; the plugin's role modules supply HOW, and the build checks the two agree one-to-one. Closed at every level: a field a later plugin needs is a reviewed schema change, and adding one is additive. Contract: engineering/decisions/2026-09-27-plugin-system.md.

name.description: The plugin's identity. The folder name and every file's `<name>.` prefix are projections the package spine checks.

api.description: The host contract this plugin is written for. A value the host does not know is a build error naming the plugin.

requires.description: Plugins this one cannot load without. A missing one, or a cycle, fails the build by name. Disabling a required plugin disables this one.

optional.description: Plugins this one uses when present and must work without.

syntax.description: markdown-it rules, keyed by the TOKEN TYPE each rule emits. The host installs them; the plugin's `<name>.syntax.mjs` exports each rule under its key (a named export per token type, so a bundler keeps only the rules a consumer imports) and its `<name>.render.js` a `renderers` object with the same keys.

diagnostics.description: Stable IDs, namespaced `<plugin>/<id>`, and the message each reports.

fences.description: Fenced code blocks this plugin renders, keyed by the fence NAME an author writes (```name). The host owns one fence table keyed by name and alias; the plugin's `<name>.render.js` exports a `fences` object with the same keys. A name or alias two plugins claim, or one a code language already owns (a highlight.js language or alias, or a host-reserved name), fails the build by name.

hydrate.description: The browser half: `<name>.hydrate.js` exports `hydrate(el, ctx)`, which turns each placeholder this plugin's fences emitted into a figure. ONE source for every browser surface — the runtime bundles it, the CLI export page runs it serialized — so the module must be self-contained: no require, no import; everything it needs arrives through `ctx`. With `render.exec.hydrate: "pass"` the module exports `createPass(ctx)` instead — a document pass the runtime drives, never serialized — and `budgetMs` does not apply.

budgetMs.description: How long one placeholder may stay pending before the host settles it final with its source text. Default 4000.

bake.description: `<name>.bake.js` exports `bake(source, ctx)`: Node-side, run by the CLI export (lib/plugins/host-bake.js) over the deck's Markdown BEFORE the engine renders it, only for a deck that uses the plugin. It draws the plugin's figures into static markup and returns the new source. Never bundled for a browser. Requires `render.exec.bake`.

highlight.description: `<name>.highlight.js` exports `highlight(hljs)`, a highlight.js language definition. The host registers it on the engine's highlight.js under each of the plugin's code fences (`as: "code"`), so the source a fence shows before it is drawn — or when it cannot be — is syntax-colored. Requires at least one code fence.

extensionPoints.description: Slots this plugin OFFERS and components FILL — the chart family's `kernel`. Keyed by the SLOT name, the plugin's own. A component fills a slot by declaring the slot's BLOCK in its manifest (`block`, default the slot name: a chart's `"kernel": { … }`), an object-typed block the component manifest schema already defines; one plugin reads a block. In api 1 a slot is filled only by IN-TREE COMPONENTS, with code: every component in `bucket` that declares the block fills it, and its `<component>.<role>.js` exports `entry`, called with the signature the offering plugin's `api` and `description` fix. Filling a slot is REQUIRING the plugin (it is loaded for a deck that uses the class, and a slide reports `plugin/component-needs-plugin` when it is not running), so the component writes no `plugins` block for it. A block two plugins read, a bucket two slots claim, or a block declared outside its slot's bucket fails the build by name. Reserved for a later version, as an additive field: a slot that PLUGINS fill (data, such as an icon pack) rather than components. In-tree only: neither offering nor filling a slot travels by zip (spec/LPM.md §10).

inline.description: Inline-code KINDS: a record behind one tag character, written in Segno's notation (`^{database, c3}`), keyed by the kind's name. The host owns one dispatch table (lib/core/inline-code-directives.js) whose first rows are its own marks, pills and sparks; it keeps the dispatch order and the backslash escape. The plugin's `<name>.inline.js` exports an `inline` object with the same keys, each `{ resolve, html, element, diagnose }`: text → fields, an HTML string, a DOM element, or why an attempt does not render. Bundled wherever the dispatcher is (the linter, the runtime), so the module must stay light: no data it can load later. A sigil another row claims (`~` is the spark's) fails the build by name. In-tree only.

sigil.description: The tag character before `{`: one of Segno's TAGS (docs/src/lib/segno/notation-grammar.ts).

services.description: Named functions other code may call through the host (lib/plugins/services.js `service(plugin, name)`), never by importing the plugin: with the plugin off, the caller gets null and renders without it. The plugin's `<name>.services.js` exports a `services` object with exactly these keys. Light, like `inline`. In-tree only.

registers.description: Front-matter registers declared as DATA, keyed by the register's key and class prefix (`icon` → `icon: bare etching` and the `icon-bare` slide classes). The host's register factory (lib/core/register-factory.js) builds each one exactly as it builds `spark:`: one word per axis, a slide's word evicting the deck's on that axis only. A prefix a first-party register owns, or a word two axes share, fails the build.

additionalProperties.description: The axis's words, its default first.

data.description: `<name>.data.generated.js` exists: plain data the plugin's kernels read through lib/plugins/plugin-data.js `pluginData(name)`, never by `require`. The engine registers a lazy loader for it (lib/plugins/data.generated.js), so a Node render loads it on first use; a browser bundle aliases that file to a stub and the data arrives as its own script (`globalThis.__latticePluginData`), fetched only for a deck that uses the plugin.

styles.description: `<name>.styles.css` exists: token-only CSS, bundled into the plugin slot of dist/lattice.css in dependency order. Every `var(--token)` it reads must be listed in `tokens`, and every listed token read.

parity.description: LPM's parity: every surface emits the same semantic contract (equivalent), or a static surface emits a skeleton a browser enriches (progressive).

degradesTo.description: What the host shows when a renderer throws or returns a non-string.

hydrate.description: `browser`: `<name>.hydrate.js` exports `hydrate(el, ctx)`, run by the plugin host on every browser surface, the CLI export page included (serialized). `pass`: `<name>.hydrate.js` exports `createPass(ctx)`, a document pass the runtime bundles and drives (boot, run, onMutations) — for a browser half that must walk every figure together, as Mermaid's per-palette render queue does. A pass is never serialized, so it may require in-tree kernels; the CLI export page carries no runtime, so such a plugin must declare `bake`. In-tree only.

bake.description: The bake drives a separate process (a headless browser, a render worker) and blocks until it returns.

figureClasses.description: The CSS classes of the container this plugin draws a figure into (on any surface: its runtime pass, its bake). They are the plugin's OWN: every consumer outside lib/plugins finds a drawn figure by the host's `data-lattice-figure` marker instead, and `checkPluginMigration`'s `drawnFigureClasses` arm counts any that names one of these (budget 0).

surfaces.description: What each surface EMITS for this plugin: `placeholder` (markup a browser fills), `figure` (the drawn result), `figure-baked` (drawn, then frozen to static markup), `source` (the author's text), `none`.

payload.description: Third-party files a browser surface loads for this plugin. `when: used` loads a file only for a deck that uses the plugin; the CLI export injects it, the runtime fetches it from beside itself by the file's basename.

from.description: The file, as `npm:<package>/<path>` — the version package-lock.json locks, never a vendored copy.

global.description: The window global the file defines; `ctx.lib` hands it to `hydrate`.

when.description: Only `used` in v1: loaded when the deck uses the plugin.

tokens.description: Every design token the plugin's CSS paints with. The build holds this list one-to-one with the `var(--…)` reads in `<name>.styles.css`.

anchor.description: Where the host installs the rule: before or after a rule the HOST names, never another plugin's.

triggers.description: The characters the rule starts on. Two plugins claiming one character is a build error; a character markdown-it's text rule does not stop at is refused, because the rule would never fire.

opaque.description: block only: the rule's body renders no inline Markdown, so lint-core skips it as it skips a code fence. (Every block rule, opaque or not, is also installed in the boundary parser, so the source-side slide splitter agrees with the render about where a slide starts.)

block.description: The component manifest block a filler declares. Default: the slot name. Name it when the slot's own name should not claim a block word for good.

bucket.description: The component bucket whose members fill the slot (`chart`). One slot per bucket.

role.description: The role of the filler's module, by the spine's `<name>.<role>.js` rule (`transform` → `bar/bar.transform.js`).

entry.description: The function that module exports and the plugin calls (`transformSection`).

description.description: What a filler supplies, the entry's signature, and what the plugin does with it.

deprecated.description: The alias still renders, and the render reports its replacement.

body.description: The language of the fence body, for the editor's highlighter and the docs.

as.description: The engine renders this fence as the code block every other fence becomes — highlighted, `class="language-<name>"` — and the plugin draws it later: its `bake` on the CLI, the runtime's own pass (`render.exec.hydrate: "runtime"`) in a browser. The fence is still the plugin's: no other plugin may claim the name, and it counts as use. `<name>.render.js` has no renderer for it, and it takes no aliases.
